articles.title: ‘He is not human’ – NFL fans cannot believe Josh Allen’s ‘miracle play’ in big win
articles.summary: One Josh Allen masterclass moment has captured the attention of NFL fans after the Buffalo Bills’ big win and most are simply awestruck by his genius. In wha...
articles.body:
One Josh Allen masterclass moment has captured the attention of NFL fans after the Buffalo Bills' big win and most are simply awestruck by his genius.

In what proved to be a tight contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Buffalo Bills claimed their fifth win of the season. The difference-maker was none other than the team's star quarterback. Josh Allen did just enough to secure the victory for his team.

Allen threw the ball for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and looked like his usual impressive self during the game. The 33-30 scoreline suggests how tight the game was. And while a game like this is generally known for having a lot of big moments, one Allen play has really captured the fans' imaginations.

Josh Allen's third quarter scramble and touchdown pass left NFL fans online in awe of his skills

With the score at 16-13 in the third quarter, Allen had the ball for the Bills at the Raiders' 13-yard line. It was third down with eight yards to gain, and it would have been bad for Buffalo if they had to settle for the field goal.

The Raiders' defensive line knew they had to get the stop if they could. They sold out to try to sack Allen, but he somehow escaped the pocket. As more Las Vegas players rushed to meet him and put him on the ground, the 30-year-old casually flipped the ball to Keon Coleman in the endzone.

"Josh Allen is something else man, he is not human," one fan wrote. "Josh Allen is the 6th grader playing with 4th graders at recess," a second fan observed. "Josh Allen is not human. This is a new level of excellence we are not worthy of," said a third fan.

"I feel like even Josh Allen is surprised by the things Josh Allen can do sometimes," a fourth fan hilariously claimed. "Give him the MVP right now," a different comment read. "He can do anything. And his receivers know that at any moment he might do something nuts, so they're always ready. It's a pleasure to watch that man apply his craft," a sixth fan said.

The vision to see that play and the talent to make it are unfathomable for most quarterbacks, even at the highest level. Allen is making a strong case for himself to be named MVP for the second time in his career, and the fans clearly think he is the best around at the moment.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Sends Message to Giants Fans After Week 6 Outing
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy sent a message to the Giants fans following the team’s Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints.Despite being the home...
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy sent a message to the Giants fans following the team's Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Despite being the home team, the Giants lost 34-27 to the Saints on Sunday. It was a tough game for New York, who took an early lead only to battle back from being down 24 points to make it close at the end, with a last-minute rally that ultimately fell short on a failed fourth-down play to seal the win for New Orleans.

Despite the tough loss, though, there are plenty of positives to take away from this game for Giants head coach John Harbaugh, including the strong play of McCarthy, who came off the bench in the second half of the game to take over for starting QB Jameis Winston and had a great showing in relief.

Despite the loss, McCarthy performed well, and the fans immediately took a liking to him, which he appreciated.

J.J. McCarthy Praises Giants Fans After Big Win

Speaking to reporters following the game, McCarthy praised the Giants fans for all of their support, showing how close the bond between the city and the player is already.

"I'm just extremely honored to be a part of the New York Football Giants, because this fanbase is unbelievable. The passion, how they show up every single game, home and away, it means the world to wear this blue and to play for them. All love to this city and the jersey, and I'm just extremely grateful for them," McCarthy said.

J.J. McCarthy Excelled Against New Orleans

Despite coming into the game in relief of a struggling Winston, McCarthy excelled during his first true opportunity to get reps for the Giants.

He was 11-for-23 in completions with 243 passing yards and one touchdown compared to one interception, and he gave the Giants a chance to win after being down big heading into the final quarter of the game, as it looked like New York was going to get blown out.

In the end, it was a loss for New York, which dropped their season record to 3-2-1, but it was still a really good showing by McCarthy, one that should give coach Harbaugh even more confidence to potentially start him going forward.

Although Harbaugh did not commit to giving McCarthy the start in the team's Week 7 game against the Houston Texans , he certainly needs to give it heavy consideration, given McCarthy's strong play in this game against the Saints and Winston's struggles overall behind center for the Giants this season.

Winston is an incredible teammate and someone whom the Giants love having around in the locker room, but he is more but he is much more suitable as a backup at this point in his NFL career.

McCarthy, meanwhile, was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and although it's been a struggle for him so far during his NFL career, he's still young enough to turn things around and show that he has what it takes to start games in this league.

articles.title: NFL Could Hand Down Punishment Over Rams Game After Controversial Call
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams could see the NFL take action following a polarizing decision against Josh Wallace in the loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The post NFL Co...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' loss to the Arizona Cardinals featured a polarizing call against cornerback Josh Wallace that could see the NFL step in.

Unfortunately for Wallace and the Rams, further discipline is among the possible outcomes.

On a first-and-10 play from the Cardinals 35-yard line, Arizona's Jacoby Brissett connected with wide receiver Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard gain. As he came down with the pass, Wallace was attempting to make the tackle, but connected with Brooks' helmet instead.

It was a blow from the shoulder. Officials still flagged Wallace for "unnecessary roughness," gifting the Cardinals 15 yards, putting them within field goal range.

There was also an offsides call against Josaiah Stewart, but the Cardinals, naturally, declined.

Rams' Josh Wallace Could Be Punished By NFL

During the game, rules analyst Mike Pereira sided with the broadcast team that the hit did not seem to meet the criteria for a flag, i.e. forcible contact to the head and or neck area. But Wallace must now be concerned that the NFL will side with the officials.

Wallace's hit could see the infraction specified as a "hit on a defenseless player." That is one of the NFL's fineable offenses.

Per the NFL , a first-time infraction can incur a fine as high as $17,911.

A second infraction could draw a fine as high as $23,882. This infraction would also count as one strike for Wallace. Two more strikes of this kind, and the third-year cornerback will trigger an automatic one-game suspension.

Wallace can appeal the fine, potentially leading to a reduction. However, the strike will carry over into future seasons if it holds.

To make matters worse, that was the only penalty called for a fineable offense in the game.

Wallace was also on the wrong side of a call against the Rams that altered their loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3. He could see history repeat itself in that regard, but the Rams are feeling that in-game decision now.

"UNREAL PERSONAL FOUL," Sharp Football Analysis' Warren Sharp posted on X in reaction to the call, including a clip.

Rams On SI's Blaine Grisak posted , "How are we calling that unnecessary roughness on Josh Wallace?" adding that is was "another penalty this season late in the fourth quarter that Wallace has been screwed on."

"Another tough call on Josh Wallace there, and I don't love it, but the Rams put themselves in this position to lose this game," Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer posted on X.

Former NFL safety Quandre Diggs posted on X that the "Rams got cheated."

Rivals' Greg Biggins posted , "The League obviously hates Josh Wallace! What a wild way to lose a game [laughing face emoji]," underscoring the incredulous response to the call that many had in real time.

Wallace was playing so much partly due to the absence of Trent McDuffie. McDuffie suffered a groin injury in practice during the week.

Wallace will look to avoid the officials' attention in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders .

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh to 'address everything' after latest loss drops Chargers to 0-6, leading to more Mike McDaniel questions
articles.summary: The Chargers "have to address everything, and especially offensively," Jim Harbaugh said on Sunday.
articles.body:
Calls for Mike McDaniels' job are only getting louder.

This time, though, Jim Harbaugh wasn't as strong in his defense of his offensive coordinator.

Harbaugh, after the Los Angeles Chargers fell 22-6 to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, said that they are going to "have to address everything, and especially offensively." The loss knocked them to 0-6 on the season, which marks their worst start since 2000. Coincidentally, Harbaugh was on that Chargers team as a player that finished 1-15 that season.

And when asked about McDaniel directly and if he was going to keep calling plays, Harbaugh said they were "going to look at everything."

"The job I'm doing, it starts with me. We'll watch this and get with our offensive coaches," Harbaugh said, via ESPN . "I see the effort, I see the work being put in in the meetings, on the practice field, and to get that to translate to the field is what's necessary. Feel bad for our players, our team, our coaches, our fans. And [offense] needs to be addressed."

The Chargers only put up six points on Sunday, a season-low. They are averaging just 15 points per game, which is better than only the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans. The Dolphins and Chargers are the only two teams in the league still without a win this season.

Justin Herbert went 22-of-37 for 204 yards with an interception. He was the team's leading rusher, too, with 26 yards. Herbert has thrown just five touchdowns to eight interceptions so far this season. He only threw 13 total interceptions last season in total.

"I don't know," Herbert said when asked what's not working for him offensively. "If I had the answers, then we'd definitely be having a different conversation."

It would take a truly historic turnaround for the Chargers to salvage this season and make the playoffs. Only one team has ever made the postseason after an 0-4 start — the Chargers did that in 1992 — but none has ever pulled that off after six straight losses.

Making a change at offensive coordinator, though, could be a first step. McDaniel is in his first season in the role after his split with the Miami Dolphins last season. He led that franchise for four seasons, and finished with just a 35-33 record.

NBC Sports' Mike Florio reported on Sunday that there is "growing buzz" that the Chargers will move on from McDaniel soon, too. When that happens, he said, former Dolphins and New York Jets head coach Adam Gase, now the Chargers' pass game specialist, would fill his role in the interim. The Chargers are entering their bye week, so it would leave them extra time to adjust to the change were they to make it now. But "soon," of course, is relative.

Simply firing McDaniel wouldn't cure everything, either. And Harbaugh isn't blaming him. They have a much bigger problem, and it starts at the top.

"There's no justification. Anything I would say would sound like an excuse. I'm opposed to that to the core and pointing fingers because I believe this is a team game," he said. "But definitely offensively, we need to evaluate and we need to look at it all — everything we're doing and how we're doing it."

articles.title: Thanks to familiar miscues, the Dallas Cowboys are off to their worst start in years
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys can’t run the ball or stop opposing offenses. Its resulted in their worst record through six games since 2020.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys don’t run the ball well. Their much-hoped-for defensive turnaround hasn’t materialized. Unable to count on either, the Cowboys have hinged their playoff hopes for a third straight season on the right arm of quarterback Dak Prescott. The result? Their worst record through six games since 2020. “The effort is right, the fight is right,” Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said. “Mistakes are killing us.” They continued in a 23-13 loss to Green Bay on “Sunday Night Football” that left the Cowboys 2-4. As they chase their first playoff berth since 2023, a lone silver lining has been the dreadful state of the NFC East, where the Cowboys aren’t out of contention thanks to the up-and-down struggles of division-leading New York (3-2-1), a rash of injuries in Philadelphia (2-4) and the regression of Washington (1-3-1). All four teams in the division have a negative scoring differential, the only division this season to do that. What makes Dallas difficult to count out was seen on the scoring drive that pulled it within 23-13 with 44 seconds to play in Sunday’s fourth quarter, after Prescott led a 13-play, 78-yard drive capped by his scramble away from two tacklers before throwing a touchdown pass on the run. Prescott’s ability, coupled with receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens — their 862 combined receiving yards entering Sunday were second-most by a duo in the league — left Dallas seventh in the league in points scored entering Week 6. Yet what makes Dallas difficult to count on was also on display just four minutes earlier in the fourth quarter. Needing 11 yards on fourth down to continue their drive and cut into a 23-7 Packers lead, Prescott narrowly avoided a sack before lofting a pass that sailed out the back of the end zone, not close to any particular Cowboys receiver. The reliance on Prescott largely paid off to begin this season, as he threw eight touchdowns against just one interception through his first four games. In the last two, though, Prescott has two touchdowns and four interceptions. The latter total doesn’t include an interception Sunday that was negated by a Green Bay penalty for roughing the passer. Dallas’ defense “played a good enough game for us to go out there and win this,” Prescott said. “We just didn’t hold our own on offense.” Struggles against Green Bay are nothing new for the Cowboys, who are 1-11-1 in their last 13 meetings against the Packers. Entering Sunday’s game, the Cowboys had allowed at least 30 points in their last six games against Green Bay, the longest streak of any team against Dallas in the franchise’s history. Yet much of what has ailed Dallas against Green Bay applies to the rest of their opponents, as well, and has left them rarely able to make consistent progress toward becoming a legitimate playoff contender. Since Cowboys defensive coordinator Dan Quinn left to coach Washington in 2023 on the heels of producing the league’s fifth-best defense, the Cowboys have been a defensive sieve, with three different coordinators in as many years. The Cowboys ranked second-to-last in scoring defense in 2024, and dead last last season before hiring Christian Parker, a first-time coordinator at any level, to design a turnaround this fall. The Cowboys memorably stopped wrecking-ball Baltimore running back Derrick Henry twice on fourth-and-short during a Week 3 win; they also have ranked second-to-last in yards allowed, and resorted to hiring the retired defensive coach Mike Pettine last week to help Parker. When Dallas linebacker Dee Winters picked off Green Bay’s Jordan Love early in the first half by anticipating a route from Matthew Golden, it was the Cowboys’s first interception this season. They were the last team to record one. Apart from that takeaway, Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love rarely looked bothered. When Dallas pressured Love on more than half of his 44 dropbacks, he completed 11 of his 19 passes, anyway. Though Green Bay’s 23 points were the second-fewest allowed by Dallas this season, the total could have easily been higher, after Packers receiver Matthew Golden dropped what appeared to be two likely touchdown receptions; after one drop, the Packers’ drive stalled and settled for a field goal. The Packers also picked apart Dallas on third down. They weren’t the only ones to do so, however. Dallas entered Week 6 allowing opponents to convert more than 52% of their third-down opportunities, the league’s highest percentage. Before his promotion last year to head coach, Schottenheimer helped design the Cowboys’ offense that has leaned heavily on Prescott; on Sunday, he attempted 54 passes, completing 34. But even the passing game that has typically been one of the league’s most productive has generated just 29 total points over its last two games. “We put ourselves in a hole,” Schottenheimer said. “There’s one way out of it.”

images.caption: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott reacts during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Dani Dennis-Sutton celebrates after a play during the first quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. Kevin Sabitus / Getty Images

articles.title: NFL London delivers drama, Los Angeles Rams face nightmare and Kenneth Walker III does it again - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams were dealt another blow to their season as they suffered a shock defeat to the Arizona Cardinals; the NFL international games continue when the New Orleans Saints face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris, France, live on Sky Sports this Sunday
articles.body:
The UK closed the curtain on its annual residency Sunday with one of the greatest game in its near-two-decade history as a regular-season host, Ka'imi Fairbairn's walk-off field goal leading the Houston Texans to a 34-31 shootout win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

A last-second kick to win it all came just a week on from Cam Little's dramatic field goal as the Jaguars stunned the Philadelphia Eagles in one of the most iconic London games moments, a Jude Bellingham celebration to match proving a textbook tip of the hat to these shores. This time, though, it was the turn of the Texans to boot their way to British bedlam.

The Wembley press box had kindly provided cookies among a selection of sweet treats for media to enjoy at half-time, and so there national and international journalists sat, alternating between munching and typing as CJ Stroud and Trevor Lawrence traded MVP credentials. Somewhere in the middle became a less cohesive not-so-excellent Corgi race just about as chaotic as a Brian Flores blitz, but perhaps it was fitting. Chaos within the chaos.

There really was no let-up, the decibels ramping up as the floodlights fended off a darkening sky, under which an exceptional Stroud continued his superb start to the campaign. He was dealing the rock with the same touch and placement that generated his Offensive Rookie of the Year acclaim in 2023, finishing with 312 yards and three touchdowns while flourishing in the face of pressure as the Jags sought to blitz him.

Stroud has now thrown for 250-plus yards in five of six games this season, having only achieved the feat three times last year. Both he and Bryce Young have faced criticism at different points since entering the league as the first two picks of their Draft class. Suddenly they are playing like two of the best quarterbacks in football.

"Our fans are right: C.J. Stroud for MVP," said Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans.

London meanwhile enjoyed a historic day for Travis Hunter as the two-position Jags star scored a touchdown and intercepted Stroud in the end zone, becoming the first player to do both in the same game since Brian Dawkins against the Texans in 2002.

A hugely successful month for the NFL in London, where you can't help but feel there is now an added pressure, perhaps expectation, to both deliver theatre and lead by the front as the rest of the globe seeks to feed off its blueprint. Paris awaits next weekend, with barnstormers in both Brazil and London having set the bar exceedingly high.

The Los Angeles Rams are staring at the reality of their nightmare coming true. They were billed as the NFL's supposed super-team, entering the season as favourites after the arrival of Myles Garrett and return of Aaron Donald with whom to bolster a unit already led by MVP Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua. On Sunday they were beaten 18-16 by Jacoby Brissett's Arizona Cardinals, falling to 2-4 at the bottom of the NFC West division. Sean McVay's side could not capitalise against a defense that arrived into Sunday's game allowing the 26th most yards per game and the most points in the NFL, scoring on just three of 10 drives while Stafford continued his uncomfortable start to the season. Having cut kicker Harrison Mevis during the week, the Rams lost his replacement Blake Grupe to injury after the former New Orleans Saint was hurt while attempting a tackle, adding to their debilitating special teams woes.

What Jeffery Simmons would do to be on a competitive team?! What we as fans of the sport would do to see it? Since being taken with the 19th overall pick of the 2019 NFL Draft, the four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle went to the AFC Championship game in his first year in the league but it's been a barren wasteland that has served as the scene for his last four - Tennessee returning a combined record of 19-49 - that then bled into an 0-5 start to this season. But a win is now finally on the board for the Titans, their first for 12 games, with Simmons the catalyst as he returned six tackles and two sacks against the Colts, while it was his forced fumble of Jonathan Taylor to start the second half that sparked the comeback victory from 13-0 down. "I thought he was outstanding in the locker room at half-time," head coach Robert Saleh said afterwards. "It may have gone unnoticed, but for me, just watching him and observing the team, he's a man's man, and I appreciate him. I think he's the best defensive tackle in the ball, period."

The Browns are the best team in the AFC North. It is a touch premature to crown them just six weeks into the season, especially with two other teams in the division tied for the same record - in the Steelers and Ravens - and with only a bye preventing the Bengals from potentially making it a full house on four wins. BUT, Cleveland crucially hold tiebreakers over Pittsburgh and Baltimore after beating both, with their 13-10 triumph over the latter on Sunday making it the deepest into a season that the Browns have held first place in their division for 12 years!

JJ McCarthy: The former Minnesota Viking - the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft - was brought in to see out the final quarter of the Giants' loss to the Saints, trailing by 24, only to almost pull off the most unlikely of comebacks. His 243 passing yards is the most-ever across an 11-minute span in NFL history and has surely secured him the starting job for the Week Seven trip to the Houston Texans? If not, you'd imagine the change will come out the back of their Week Eight bye.

Kenneth Walker III: He might be the league MVP through six weeks. Kenneth Walker III continues to make the Chiefs tick, rushing for 128 yards and two touchdowns as Andy Reid's side beat the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 to improve to 5-0 on the year. The Chiefs running back forced seven more missed tackles to increase his tally to a league-leading 52, according to NextGenStats. He meanwhile leads the NFL in yards and touchdowns from runs against stacked boxes; put all the men you want against him - he is still finding ways to win.

Nick Sirianni: Jordan Mailata said he had endured the 'week from hell' after the Eagles saw Lane Johnson retire before trading Cam Jurgens to the Ravens and then losing dramatically in London. It got even worse for Nick Sirianni this week as Philly placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve with a blood clot, before losing 25-14 to the Carolina Panthers to drop to 2-4. The Eagles are creeping towards turmoil now, and a bleak conclusion awaits Sirianni at this rate.

Mike McCarthy : It wasn't exactly a red-letter day for all McCarthys in the NFL. JJ's namesake, the head coach of the Steelers, suffered the embarrassment of missing his half-time team talk due to an apparent ankle injury that forced him into the injury tent for further assessment. He did manage to return to the sideline for the second half and oversee a Pittsburgh victory in Tampa Bay - but one that came at a cost!

Player of the Weekend - Kyler Gordon, DB, Chicago Bears

What a way to mark your return. Bears defensive back Kyler Gordon played in his first game of the season on Sunday, by the end of which he had recorded three sacks, three tackles for loss, two quarterback hits and two forced fumbles in Chicago's 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. He is a difference maker at multiple levels for this Bears defense. Caleb Williams impressed on his return from injury by completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown, marking the highest completion rate by a Bears quarterback to attempt at least 30 passes in team history, according to NFL Network. But this was Gordon's game.

London probably did claim the Game of the Weekend with Houston's win over Jacksonville, but beyond our headline story the Buffalo Bills held off the Las Vegas Raiders in a 33-30 to get to 5-1 on the year. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns to tie Jim Kelly's franchise record of 258 touchdown passes, including his improvised shot-putt strike to Keon Coleman in true Allen fashion. James Cook, so often a driving force for the Bills offense, delivered a defining contribution down the stretch with a three-yard rushing touchdown with 4.43 left to reward his own 26-yard sideline scamper. Tyler Bass then scored a 38-yard field goal inside the two-minute warning to make it a two-possession lead, ultimately negating Tre Tucker's 44-yard touchdown on the ensuing drive.

articles.title: NFL Week 6: The return of Caleb Williams, and life gets worse for the Rams
articles.summary: Week 6 of the NFL season featured a star player returning from one the season’s most dramatic injuries, an important game across the pond, and another devastating loss for a Super Bowl contender.
articles.body: Week 6 of the NFL season featured a star player returning from one the season’s most dramatic injuries, an important game across the pond, and another devastating loss for a Super Bowl contender. Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday. Caleb Williams picked up where he left off Chicago Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams played Sunday for the first time since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 2, and he was spectacular in a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and one touchdown, improving his completion percentage to 72.5% for the season. Williams was especially efficient when not facing pressure. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Williams completed all 24 of his passes from a clean pocket, the most attempts without an incompletion under such circumstances since 2018. After going 2-1 without their starter, the Bears improved to 4-2 with the win. The offense has been humming with Williams under center, averaging 31.0 points per game in his three starts. Chicago will now enter a spotlighted stretch of its season, as the team’s next three games will all be played in primetime. The Rams are still searching for answers Six weeks after entering the season as a heavy favorite to win the Super Bowl, the Los Angeles Rams (2-4) are in last place in the NFC West after Sunday’s 18-16 home loss to the Arizona Cardinals. After a frustrating day with little offense, the Rams had finally pieced together a productive drive to tie the game at 15-all in the fourth-quarter’s final minute. The point-after was no foregone conclusion. The team cut kicker Harrison Mevis after a miss in last week’s loss to Buffalo, only to see his replacement, Blake Grupe, get hurt trying to make a tackle early Sunday. That left Rams punter Ethan Evans to step up to attempt his first point-after since college — which he made to give Los Angeles a one-point lead with 47 seconds left. It was a different kicker who ended up the hero, though. A controversial penalty on the Rams for unnecessary roughness — a penalty that increased the Cardinals’ win probability from 26% to 74% — helped Arizona’s final drive move downfield in position for Chad Ryland to attempt a game-winning kick from 43 yards. He nailed it to keep the Rams still looking for any consistency. By the way: The Rams and Chargers have one win combined inside their home stadium, SoFi Stadium, this season. The Cardinals are 2-0 there. The Texans’ season isn’t over just yet The Houston Texans are winners of two straight after a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. This was the first game of the day on Sunday, and perhaps the best. Quarterbacks C.J. Stroud and Trevor Lawrence combined for 618 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Stroud was nearly perfect, posting a quarterback rating of 96.9 (out of a possible 100). After the Texans opened up a 10-point lead in the final minute of the third quarter, the Jaguars stormed back. First, Lawrence led a nine-play, 61-yard touchdown drive to cut the score to 31-28 early in the fourth. Then, after a Travis Hunter interception, Lawrence led a 38-yard drive that culminated in a 60-yard field goal from Cam Little. But Houston got the last laugh. After Little’s kick, the Texans quickly marched into Jacksonville territory on their ensuing possession. Ka’imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired, securing Houston’s second win of the season. The Texans are now 2-4, and while their climb into playoff position will be an arduous one, Houston did make the postseason after an 0-3 start a year ago. If Stroud maintains his current level of play — he’s thrown nine touchdowns and only one interception so far this season — the Texans won’t be a pushover. The Titans rose from the ranks of the winless Tennessee’s season-long nightmare is finally over. The Titans finally won a game, knocking off their divisional rival the Indianapolis Colts 26-20. Tennessee stormed back in the second half, scoring all of its points in the final 30 minutes, including 20 in the final quarter. The Colts aided the cause with a litany of mistakes. Quarterback Daniel Jones threw two interceptions, running back Jonathan Taylor had a fumble, the special teams had a punt blocked for a touchdown, and the offense also had a turnover on downs for good measure. The Titans are now 1-5. Indianapolis, meanwhile, entered this season with high expectations from ownership, but fell to 2-4 after the loss.

articles.body: We let it go when the Los Angeles Rams didn't immediately get signature offseason addition Myles Garrett help for his troubled knee during training camp and waited until a season-opening performance he called "the worst version of myself" to finally get the matter addressed. Garrett is now eligible to return from the injured reserve list but there is no absolute certainty that will happen this week following his Sept. 14 surgery. We also looked the other way when the Rams took their travel scheduling advice to Australia from an Instagram trip planner (not really, it was coach Sean McVay) and were sluggish and generally a step slow in the season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers because they traveled across the planet 36 hours before a game while the 49ers spent a week in Australia acclimating. We cannot forget or forgive the 18-16 loss to the upstart Arizona Cardinals. At home. Marking a second consecutive loss at SoFi Stadium. The Rams are now trolling the people who picked them as the Super Bowl favorites before the season began. They're making us — yes, me included – look dumb as they've piled curious, questionable, disappointing things atop each other en route to last place in the NFC West. Their quarterback was the NFL's MVP last season. So, you're darn right us dummies picked them as a Super Bowl fave. But that logical choice came with the inconvenient fact that teams must actually play games to prove their worth. And the Rams have not only failed to do that, but failed in epic fashion. This is a club that held a 16-0 halftime lead against the Denver Broncos in Week 3 and collapsed in the second half on the way to a 30-26 loss. articles.title: NFL Week 6 Sunday takeaways: Giants have a new QB1, Bills keep rolling and Shane Steichen is on the hot seat
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy sparked a Giants quarterback controversy with a furious NFL Week 6 comeback, while the Browns climbed into first in the AFC North.
articles.body: Six weeks into the NFL season, the Giants and Browns are in first place, the Eagles should probably start thinking about next year, and I'm still not buying the Jaguars hype. Just a perfectly normal Sunday. We also got a reminder that a big fourth-quarter lead is only comfortable until your team decides to stop playing football. The Bears nearly turned a blowout into a disaster, and the Giants somehow went from getting embarrassed to creating a quarterback controversy. If you figured either game was over early and changed the channel, I can't blame you. But you missed a few things. Here's my biggest takeaway from each game on the Week 6 Sunday slate. Texans 34, Jaguars 31 Takeaway: I tried to warn y'all about jumping on the Jaguars bandwagon. Look, this isn't to say Jacksonville isn't a solid team. But the media was very quick to anoint them as a major contender in the AFC. I've said many times that this team isn't nearly as good as everyone thinks, and that showed against the 1-4 Texans. Jacksonville even had the advantage of already being in London, while Houston had to travel across the pond this week. FORMER NFL QB SEAN SALISBURY WANTS OFFICIALS TO FACE POSTGAME QUESTIONS LIKE PLAYERS AND COACHES The Jaguars allowed C.J. Stroud to throw for 312 yards and three touchdowns. Trevor Lawrence is definitely playing some of the best football of his career and the Jags are the best team in the AFC South. But they're not a true AFC Championship contender right now. Browns 13, Ravens 10 Takeaway: Don't look now, but the Browns are in first place. Well, kinda. With the upset win over the Ravens, Cleveland moves to 4-2 and into a tie with Baltimore and Pittsburgh. Yes, the Ravens were missing Lamar Jackson, but this was a huge win for the Browns. I don't think many people, myself included, would have predicted that Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns would be 4-2 and tied for the AFC North lead after six games. Watson only threw for 164 yards and he still doesn't look that good, but, as the great philosopher Bill Parcells once said, "You are what your record says you are." Right now, it says the Browns are 4-2. Saints 34, Giants 27 Takeaway: There's a new QB1 in New York. Jameis Winston showed some of that Jameis magic in Week 5 when he led the team from two touchdowns down in the second half to force overtime and eventually a tie against the Commanders. But the magic wasn't there in Week 6. Winston threw two interceptions before New York turned to the recently acquired J.J. McCarthy … who promptly threw an interception of his own. But even after the rough start, McCarthy rebounded to lead three consecutive scoring drives, cutting the 34-10 deficit to 34-27. He finished with 243 passing yards and a touchdown pass in just over 11 minutes. He even moved the team to the Saints' 14-yard line in the final seconds, but couldn't quite make the game-tying play. Still, it's pretty clear that this team (which is in first place, by the way) has to give the reins to McCarthy moving forward. Titans 26, Colts 20 Takeaway: Shane Steichen's seat should be red hot. Losing to the previously winless Tennessee Titans at home is nearly a fireable offense on its own, especially when your team had a 13-0 lead at halftime. Last season, Steichen could point to Daniel Jones' season-ending Achilles tear in Week 14 last year as the Colts' season unraveled. This year, Jones is healthy and playing as badly as he did at times with the Giants. Jones threw two picks and was sacked six times. The offensive line struggled, but Jones holding the ball too long didn't help. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Panthers 25, Eagles 14 Takeaway: I want to feel bad for Nick Sirianni, but I don't. The Eagles placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve Saturday because of a superficial blood clot in his calf, sidelining him for at least four games. His health is obviously the priority, and his absence isn't Sirianni's fault. And yes, playing with a backup QB is always tough. But scoring just 14 points against a Carolina defense that allowed 59 points earlier this season is not good enough. This is a Philadelphia team that should already be looking ahead to 2027, but whether Sirianni is still the head coach next year remains to be seen. My money is on no. Patriots 26, Jets 19 Takeaway: The Patriots still don't look like the defending AFC champions. Yes, the Patriots won. But it wasn't particularly pretty. They let the Jets hang around for most of the game, thanks in large part to two costly fumbles. Drake Maye is looking more comfortable as the season goes along, but a team like the Patriots shouldn't have this tough a time with the Jets at home. The defense clamped down in the red zone and on two crucial fourth-down plays, but still allowed New York to gain 324 yards. Bears 31, Falcons 23 Takeaway: The Bears have to finish better than that if they want to be true NFC contenders. The NFC is starting to look wide open beyond the unbeaten 49ers, and the Bears have a chance to make a run. But head coach Ben Johnson isn't going to be happy that his team nearly blew a 24-point lead with just over 12 minutes to go. Not only did the defense allow two quick touchdowns (and two two-point conversions), including one on a 91-yard drive that took just 2:38, but the offense went three-and-out, fumble, three-and-out on three consecutive fourth-quarter possessions. Atlanta had the ball with a chance to tie, and the defense redeemed itself with a strip-sack, but it got a little too close for comfort. Johnson had pulled most of his starting defense with Thursday night's game against the Patriots in mind, but this should serve as a reminder to the second-year head coach that the game isn't over until it's over. Steelers 26, Buccaneers 19 (OT) Takeaway: Teams should stop electing to kick off in overtime. I understand the strategy of wanting to know what the other team does before you get the ball. Here's the problem: regular-season overtime is only 10 minutes. The Bucs became the latest team to kick off and then watch their opponent run nearly seven minutes off the clock before scoring a touchdown. The Steelers got to run their normal offense, while Tampa Bay was forced into a must-throw hurry-up offense. Plus, if overtime becomes a three-possession period, the receiving team has the advantage. Adding it all up, it should be clear that receiving the ball in OT is the correct decision. Cardinals 18, Rams 16 Takeaway: So much for the superteam. Look, I still think the Los Angeles Rams are a good football team. But, as I wrote earlier, "you are what your record says you are." Right now, their 2-4 record doesn't say anything good about the preseason Super Bowl favorites. The Rams are too talented to struggle all season, but they should have serious concerns about the offensive line. Matthew Stafford was under duress all game, and he struggled badly when pressured, as he has all year. The upcoming schedule isn't overly difficult, so they can turn it around, but they did just lose to the Cardinals, so the opponents might not matter as much as the Rams would like. Yes, another questionable call helped cost the Rams a win. But it's their own fault for being in that position against a team that entered with one win. RAMS HAVE LEGITIMATE GRIPE WITH NFL OFFICIALS, BUT 2-4 RECORD IS A BIGGER PROBLEM Bills 33, Raiders 30 Takeaway: Josh Allen is a magician. If you didn't see Allen's ridiculous touchdown pass to Keon Coleman, I suggest you go take a look. The 2024 NFL MVP is in MVP form again this season, and the Bills are 5-1 and leading the AFC East. This is a good win for a Buffalo team that is wrapping up a two-game trip out West, beating the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams and the better-than-expected Raiders. But, as we know, Allen's career isn't defined by his regular-season success. Buffalo is well on its way to another playoff berth, and Allen needs to finally break through and lead his team to the Super Bowl. Chiefs 22, Chargers 6 Takeaway: Do Chargers fans miss Brandon Staley yet? I kid. Sort of. But Staley was hated and run out of Los Angeles after posting a 24-24 regular-season record and zero playoff wins in nearly three seasons. Jim Harbaugh was hired to much fanfare, but he's now 22-18 in the regular season with zero playoff wins as the Chargers head coach. And it doesn't look like he's going to win a playoff game this year, since Los Angeles is basically out of it in Week 6. Say what you want about Staley, but none of his three Chargers teams started 0-6. Packers 23, Cowboys 13 Takeaway: The Cowboys are all hype, no bite... again. Feels like every year we hear, "This is going to be the Cowboys' year!" And, every year, it isn't. Dallas had a ton of hype surrounding it in the preseason, per usual, but this season actually felt a little different. Dallas used two first-round picks on safety Caleb Downs and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence to try to fix a defense that was basically a sieve in 2025. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD But every game it seems one unit shows up, and the other doesn't. For the second straight week, it was the offense pulling a no-show. This is a unit that features two-star receivers, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, so there's no excuse for that. It's particularly embarrassing against a Packers defense that was missing several key starters and that had allowed at least 30 points twice this season. Before Sunday, the Packers had held three opponents under 20 points. Those teams' starting quarterbacks: Geno Smith, Jalon Daniels and Case Keenum. Well, now we can add Dak Prescott to that list.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' NFL Week 6 Game vs. Raiders
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have hit their bye week with a 5-1 record and possession of the top spot in the AFC East.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have hit their bye week with a 5-1 record and possession of the top spot in the AFC East.

That stems from Buffalo going 2-0 on a western road trip that concluded with a 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday afternoon in Nevada.

Here are my grades for all of the key players from the victory.

It wasn't a typical lights-out, dual-effort performance from the 30-year-old star, who did very little with his legs and had some red-zone misses that could have been costly had the Bills not pulled out the victory (including a forced ball to Dalton Kincaid that should have been intercepted).

That said, one of the league's top improvisers also gave us one of the plays of the year to date on a third-down touchdown "throw" to Keon Coleman that might have been the longest shovel pass in NFL history.

And while the numbers weren't mega, he did a lot of maneuvering in the pocket that didn't show up in the box score but kept Buffalo in control of this game.

It wasn't an all-timer, but it was an example of a great player finding ways to lead his team to victory.

With the pressure ramped up and his ball-security issues under the microscope, it was a splendid performance from Cook, who gained 153 scrimmage yards on 26 touches. And, most importantly, he didn't fumble.

In fact, with what appeared to be a modified death grip on the ball, the three-time Pro Bowler didn't come close to coughing the ball up.

That alone isn't the standard for a good running back showing these days, but Cook deserves credit for bouncing back in a major way from a tough spot after nearly blowing the game for this team Monday night against the Rams.

The fact that he was also the team's most efficient skill player in this game is the icing on the cake.

He did his job with two catches on a scoring drive to open the game, but then we never heard from Johnson again.

With DJ Moore again unavailable, Coleman stepped up with four receptions for a team-high 59 yards. He's now scored three touchdowns in as many weeks and has become one of the most clutch performers on this team.

Coleman has developed special chemistry with Allen, which was on display with that improvised 12-yard shovel-pass touchdown. Beyond that, he moved the sticks with great plays on scoring drives in the second, third and fourth quarters.

Shakir's second-quarter touchdown catch-and-run was just nifty, and he was a YAC hero on a 16-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter. He wasn't a major factor but contributed in some key spots and finished with four grabs and no glaring mistakes.

All of Palmer's 37 yards came on one catch in which he was wide open against what appeared to be blown coverage. You can't fault him for capitalizing on that, but he deserves heat for what could have been a costly drop late in the fourth quarter.

The rookie was generally a ghost despite playing 30 snaps. He was targeted just once and didn't make the catch, and he was penalized for an illegal shift on a second-quarter scoring drive.

After being held to just four catches in his previous three games, Kincaid rebounded with seven receptions on eight targets against the Raiders. None of them went for 15 yards, but he found a way to be a significant asset overall.

It could have been a bigger 27th birthday showing had a penalty not wiped out his third-quarter touchdown, had Allen seen him wide open downfield right after Dorian Williams' pick in the third quarter, and had he not left the game temporarily due to injury in the second half.

Knox was fine as a blocker but a non-factor in the passing game over 47 snaps. He did get open in the end zone on a third-quarter red-zone possession, but Allen didn't see him.

Good work in the running game, but that was about it over 25 snaps as Hawes blew up Buffalo's second drive with a brutal false-start penalty.

It was a fairly clean game for the 10-year veteran. He probably could have done more to help out on a first-quarter sack resulting from a zero blitz, but he did a tremendous job allowing Allen to move out of the pocket in pressure situations and delivered several key blocks in run defense.

Tremendous work from Anderson as a downfield blocker on Shakir's touchdown play. He's turning into a top-notch run blocker, but he did give up several pressures on Allen throughout the day and got away with a pretty blatant hold in the first half.

It was McGovern who primarily paved the way on back-to-back plus runs from Cook to spark Buffalo's first touchdown drive of the game. He gave up no obvious pressures, and it was he and Dawkins who made the biggest impact when half the offense carried Cook into the end zone for what was ultimately the game-winning score.

It was a bit of an off day for Buffalo's best interior offensive lineman through the first five weeks. I'd put a lot of that first-quarter sack on him, and he was later destroyed by Maxx Crosby in a big red-zone situation. Oh, and he cost Kincaid a touchdown with a third-quarter holding penalty.

Returning from a back injury, the six-year veteran was dominated by Crosby on a Kwity Paye sack that forced a punt and gave the Raiders a shot at a double-dip late in the first half. It was clean beyond that.

He left the game for a while with a rib injury and ultimately played just 21 snaps. Still, Chubb was a non-factor when he was on the field.

Rousseau had a critical pressure to secure a key three-and-out with Buffalo trailing in the second quarter and an even more important pass deflection with the game on the line in the fourth quarter. But beyond that and a couple of other hurries, he was quiet.

Walker also made a great play on Mike Washington to set the tone on that second-quarter three-and-out. He then drew a ton of attention to free up the pass rush on a key third-quarter stand and later had a monster stop on Ashton Jeanty. His impact goes far beyond the stat sheet.

His one high-impact pressure, which came in the third quarter, was mainly the result of Walker's work. Quiet day for the Week 5 standout.

For a guy who isn't on the field close to full time, Carter is in on a lot of tackles and stops. I thought he did a great job against the run across 27 snaps. This rotation is sweet.

He made one of the biggest defensive plays of the game by single-handedly shutting down Jeanty for a three-yard loss to spark a fourth-quarter goal-line stand. It was a strong overall performance across 25 snaps for the 30-year-old.

This might have been Bernard's best game of the season, which isn't saying a lot but still indicates some progress. He continues to be a liability in coverage and in open space but made a positive impact snuffing out run plays for much of the day against Las Vegas. Jim Leonhard has to put the 27-year-old in bad spots less often.

An interception is an interception, even if Williams didn't move an inch and let Kirk Cousins make a bad decision on that third-quarter pick. He still had to catch the ball! Outside of that, Williams was a complete liability on the Raiders' first touchdown drive and was routinely trucked in run defense. Nobody on this team leaves me scratching my head as much as Williams.

Often matched up with one of the best receivers in the league, Benford gave up underneath stuff all night but was not burned deep. He had great coverage on Davante Adams to force a punt in a key spot in the second half, and his tackling was stellar. It wasn't pristine, but it was his best performance thus far in 2026.

It's a work in progress for the rookie second-round pick, who faced a really tough task and was predictably inconsistent. His tackling was sharp, though, and he made two strong plays in overtime. Kudos for the versatility.

The second-year first-round pick is falling out of favor fast. He played just 17 snaps in this one, but he blew an assignment on a big Tyler Higbee catch and missed a tackle.

The veteran actually had a great first quarter or so, but Adams beat him easily on L.A.'s first touchdown and it was downhill from there. He later took an unnecessary roughness penalty and missed time with an injury, and he did more harm than good in the fourth quarter and overtime. It's hit-or-miss with this guy.

Missed tackles and poor angles once again plagued Bishop, who also struggled in coverage and reacted too slowly in zone defense. The regression continues.

This was actually a really strong tackling performance, and he limited the damage in coverage. Not bad for his most active game of the season.

You really don't want Hamlin in too many coverage situations. He easily loses positioning in zone, and the defense was lucky Cousins didn't spot Bowers after Hamlin failed to stick with him in the end zone on a third-down play in the fourth quarter.

That said, he was again a steady tackler who contributed positively in run defense and wasn't burned badly in a pinch on Sunday.

The veteran was 4-for-4 on field goals and 3-for-3 on extra points, and that 47-yarder in the fourth quarter was clutch.

The rookie wasn't asked to do much, but a 51-yarder inside the 10-yard line in the fourth quarter was more evidence that Buffalo has found its long-term punter.

For the second week in a row, Davis had a huge return to start the game. He wasn't a factor beyond that, but it was a mistake-free performance on five combined touches as a rusher, receiver and returner.

He had two strong punt returns, both of which led to scoring drives in the second half of a close game.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 6 Game vs. Ravens
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns defense was as dominant as could be for three quarters. The Cleveland Browns offense did just enough for one half.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns defense was as dominant as could be for three quarters. The Cleveland Browns offense did just enough for one half.

The result is a 4-2 Browns team picking up a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens.

The defense gave up 10 points to a Tyler Huntley-led Ravens offense, but settled in to play three shutout quarters. The offense finally decided to contribute in the second half and set up a 37-yard field goal as time expired.

Let's take a look at how it all went down and hand out some grades to the key players from Sunday afternoon.

He was slow to make decisions. Slow in running the ball and slow to decide to make just enough clutch plays to lead the game-winning drive.

Watson ended up taking five sacks on the game. It was a combination of his offensive line and the aforementioned speed with which he made decisions.

Yet, he connected with Jerry Jeudy of all people on a 33-yard strike on 3rd and 5 with under a minute to go. He made a few plays with his feet en route to a 10-play 62-yard drive to run out the final two minutes with a game-winning field goal.

That's just enough to keep him in the C range despite going 16-of-26 for 164 yards on the afternoon.

All things considered, Jaleel McLaughlin filled in admirably. The Browns run game has been disappointing all season and McLaughlin had to step in as the primary rusher with Quinshon Judkins, Raheim Sanders and Dylan Sampson all out with injuries.

His 4.6 yards per carry was actually an improvement over what Judkins has done most weeks. He also made a few key blocks in pass protection to buy Watson an extra second.

Estime's final stat line doesn't look great (nine carries, 19 yards), but he punched it in from two yards out to score the only offensive touchdown on the day.

Concepcion still hasn't put up a breakout performance, but he does his job as the Browns chain-moving wide receiver. He caught four of his six targets for 37 yards.

He also gets bonus points for holding on to the ball when he decided to tuck and run the double pass. The trick play was covered and forcing the ball could have gotten ugly quick.

Boston has been the team's most explosive receiver all season. He offered little in that department this week. He had a ball ripped out of his hands on 3rd and 5 in the fourth quarter. He had a catch for 15 yards on five targets.

Don't look now, but Jerry Jeudy came through in the clutch for the second time in the last three weeks. He came open on a dig on a 3rd-and-5 to move the chains with a huge 33-yard gain in the final drive of the game.

It was a crucial catch and boosted his final line to four catches on four targets for 69 yards.

Fannin was just about a non-factor in this one. He caught just one pass for nine yards, although his lack or production wasn't completely on him.

The Ravens sniffed out a designed screen to him and Watson had to kill the play. It is worth noting that he set up a fourth-and-1 with his nine yard catch in the third quarter. The Browns went on to convert, so his only catch was important for sustaining that drive.

Fano drew a tough matchup against Trey Hendrickson and had some struggles. Those came to a head when the veteran pass-rusher was able to work inside and Fano was slow to recover and gave up a sack on a 3rd-and-4.

Johnson was pretty solid for most of the afternoon. The lowlight was a sack that he gave up to Calais Campbell, but Watson didn't get the ball out quickly enough so it wasn't all on him.

The Ravens defense put Jenkins in tough situations multiple times. He was the primary culprit behind the sack that Nnamdi Madubuike and Tavius Robinson split in the third quarter. He tried to replace a pulling Austin Barber and was immediately driven into Watson's lap.

Barber was a bright spot on the offensive line. He wasn't at fault for any of the team's sacks and put together a nice bounceback performance after struggling against the Jets last week.

This was Howard's best game as a Cleveland Brown. He seems to have addressed his false start issues for the second week in a row. He took care of business after struggling against David Bailey last week.

Those just judging by Verse's sack production will still be frustrated, but the reality is that Verse was a huge reason for the success of the defense Sunday. Derrick Henry loves running outside zone and Verse was setting the edge like a menace throughout the game.

The pass production might be disappointing, but Verse was elite against the run.

McGuire was the Browns best pass-rushing edge defender. He joined the sack party with an untouched quarterback takedown coming off the backside edge of the Ravens ' protection scheme.

Barnett and Williams did a fine job as the rotational edges. They shared that responsibility and put some pressure on Tyler Huntley even if neither registered a sack.

Huntington keeps playing a pivotal role with Mason Graham out of the lineup. The interior rusher didn't quite get a sack, but he logged three quarterback hits on Huntley and was beating the block in front of him with quickness.

Collins had a nice secondary inside move to get his lone sack of the game. It wasn't his only time getting pressure on the quarterback, though. He continues to be difficult for guards and centers to block on the inside.

Kamara was asked to play way more snaps than usual on Sunday. He didn't look out of place, though. He was a standout in slowing down Derrick Henry with a couple of run stops on the afternoon.

It doesn't get much better for an off-ball linebacker than what Carson Schwesinger did on Sunday. He finished with 13 total tackles and forced the fumble against Derrick Henry that turned momentum the Browns' way in the fourth quarter.

Schwesinger's sideline-to-sideline speed was huge in shutting down the run game and every tackle he made in the run game was a successful play for Cleveland, per Next Gen Stats .

Schwesinger's running mate wasn't too far behind him. His presence as a blitzer was huge. He notched a sack and two quarterback hits. He became a key chess piece when defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg was dialing up pressures on third downs.

The pass rush will get a lot of credit for the win, but the secondary did their job most of the day too. Ward had a nice bounce-back game after an uncharacteristically bad one last week.

He gave up no big plays on the day and had a batted pass. The only negative was a dropped interception that could have helped the cause.

The Ravens didn't test Campbell much and he got a hand on one of the few targets that went his way.

Harden has been inconsistent for much of the season. Sunday was not some of his best work. He got beat trying to track Zay Flowers across the field on a 3rd-and-11 in the third quarter.

Still, Flowers beats a nickel just about every week and Harden managed two passes defended.

Delpit doesn't get a grade due to injury. He left in the first quarter and was ruled out with a concussion . The injury led to a lot more playing time for Emmanuel McNeil-Warren.

Hickman was fine as a tackler, making a few stops in space that could have gone for much bigger gains. He wasn't picked on in coverage, either.

The rookie got called into more action after Grant Delpit left the game with a concussion. He made the most of the opportunity with six tackles, including a tackle for a loss and a pass defensed.

He looked right at home in the team's base defense.

Szmyt, of course, gets credit for kicking the game-winning field goal as time expired. However, he also gets dinged for going wide left on the 48-yard field goal that would have given them the lead with under four minutes.

articles.title: Travis Hunter's Wife Leanna Calls Out Shannon Sharpe in IG Photo, Hall of Famer Reacts in New Video
articles.summary: The wife of Jacksonville Jaguars star Travis Hunter called out NFL Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe after Hunter's big day, and the retired tight end offered his response.
articles.body:
The wife of Jacksonville Jaguars star Travis Hunter called out NFL Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe after Hunter's big day, and the retired tight end offered his response.

Hunter caught a touchdown pass and intercepted a pass in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans, something that hadn't been done in an NFL game since 2002.

In a pair of Instagram Stories, Leanna Hunter mocked those who said the 2024 Heisman Trophy winner couldn't be a two-way player and called out Sharpe specifically: "Anyways … @shannonsharpe84 When you speak about my husband make sure you put 'TWO WAY' player in front."

Sharpe countered on his Nightcap podcast that Hunter's performance only reinforced what he had said before. He believes the second-year player is an "every-down corner" who can be utilized situationally as a wide receiver:

In Sharpe's defense, that's exactly what happened Sunday. According to Pro Football Reference , Hunter logged 62 snaps on defense to only nine on offense. He just happened to make the most of his time as a wideout, catching four passes for 59 yards and the one score.

There simply isn't a modern precedent for an NFL player having a full-time role on both sides of the ball. The closest examples were players who had one designated position and filled in at a second through necessity or a strategic gimmick.

Logging 100-plus snaps for 17 games is a recipe to have a short career. People have raised this concern for Hunter since he was in college.

Even if he doesn't have an even split between receiver and corner, the 2025 first-round pick can still be a one-of-a-kind talent if he excels on defense while being an effective pass-catcher on a limited basis.

articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson posted an apology for spitting toward members of the Las Vegas Raiders in Sunday's 33-30 win.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson posted an apology for spitting toward members of the Las Vegas Raiders in Sunday's 33-30 win.

Gardner-Johnson was ejected in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct. The CBS broadcast caught the offending action that warranted an early exit:

He followed up on Instagram after the game to "sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me."

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he said. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game."

ESPN's Adam Schefter later noted the NFL will review the incident:

Gardner-Johnson had said in the locker room immediately after the victory that he failed to control his emotions in the moment:

Providing some context for what preceded the spitting, the veteran defensive back said he and Raiders tight end Brock Bowers "were just arguing and talking."

"It was nothing negative. He ain't do nothing to me," he told reporters . "It was just in the heat of the game arguing and talking s--t. That gesture isn't warranted."

Gardner-Johnson added he's expecting the NFL to levy a fine. Following a similar incident last season, Philadelphia Eagles star Jalen Carter avoided a suspension and instead wrote a $57,222 check to the league office.

Gardner-Johnson is in his first season with the Bills, having signed a one-year, $3.5 million deal. They're his sixth team across eight seasons in the NFL.

The 28-year-old has started in each of Buffalo's first six games, recording 26 combined tackles, one interception and two pass breakups.

articles.title: 49ers' Brock Purdy Says He's Not Josh Allen, Burrow and What He Must Do When 'I Can't Always See'
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has never let his physical limitations hold him back, but he's had to go the extra mile to overcome them.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has never let his physical limitations hold him back, but he's had to go the extra mile to overcome them.

While speaking to ESPN's Nick Wagoner ahead of San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football , Purdy explained how he's navigated being an undersized signal-caller.

"I'm not the Josh Allen- or Joe Burrow-type quarterbacks where they're really big and you'd think they could [see the whole field better]," the 6'1" Purdy told Wagoner. "But I have to take everything into account. … That's why I'm huge on like, 'This receiver's taking eight steps and he's breaking to daylight on this coverage. I know this hole's going to be there.' And taking those kinds of things into factor because I can't always see."

Purdy has adopted vision training methods that extend beyond the 49ers' practice facility. Wagoner reported that the 26-year-old "spends a little time each day of the offseason" trying to improve his vision, whether he's at home in Nashville, Tennessee, or training in Florida.

"Equipped with an iPad and 3D glasses, he watches two squares move in, out and around," Wagoner detailed. "His job is to identify how and when those squares converge and diverge with his eyes moving in and out rapidly."

Wagoner added that Purdy "also does daily work with saccades, a rapid eye movement exercise in which he must follow arrows that pop up all over a screen and touch the correct one when prompted." These sessions are meant to "force him to process movement and information as fast as possible while improving his depth perception."

Purdy made it clear that he feels his vision training has been beneficial to his career, and the 49ers' 5-0 start to this season is proof that things are paying off.

"All those things help me just work on my eyesight, my eyes moving, being quick with my eyes, making quick decisions," Purdy said. "And then it records my decision-making, how fast, the percentage of getting right and wrong. I do think it helps."

articles.title: Is Dan Quinn’s job (really) in jeopardy vs. 49ers? - Commanders links
articles.summary: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn’s job security is in question vs. 49ers. But is it really in jeopardy? ESPN weighs in.
articles.body:
Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn sat at a table deep inside Northwest Stadium, trying to make sense of a moment that made none. A coach known for wearing his hat backward instead wore a look of disbelief.

For the next 10 minutes, he tried to get comfortable. He folded his arms, then put them at his side, then put them back on the table. There was no comfort, not with what he had to address.

He took a quick deep breath after the first two questions, then readied for more. And more would come. There was no getting around what happened: a botched final sequence in his team's Week 5 matchup with the New York Giants prevented a game-winning field goal attempt on the final play, resulting in a 27-27 tie.

Inside the hushed locker room afterward, receiver Terry McLaurin stood against a burgundy cement wall. He looked upset; he looked drained; he looked bewildered. McLaurin, in his eighth season with the franchise, thought he'd seen it all in Washington — but last Sunday brought something new.

With 50 seconds remaining in overtime, the Commanders had the ball at the Giants' 24-yard line with no timeouts. Then, all hell broke loose. They didn't snap the ball until there were 12 seconds to play. On the play, quarterback Jayden Daniels dropped back to pass and then quickly looked to scramble. He started upfield, then was tackled with nine seconds left. He did not get off the ground for another four seconds and there was little urgency by his teammates.

The nature of playing on "Monday Night Football" means that — by the time the pregame show arrives — the developments from the previous Sunday of wall-to-wall pigskin has been parsed and dissected, and all that remains to talk about are the two opponents that night and any recent developments around them.

This particular Monday night, that leaves only the undefeated San Francisco 49ers and the visiting Washington Commanders. The topic, then, has to be what might be the most examined sack-for-no-yards-lost in NFL history: the final play of the Commanders' confounding 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, in which quarterback Jayden Daniels, with no timeouts, took a snap with a dozen seconds left, was tackled with eight ticks remaining — and never got another snap off.

"Ultimately, it's on me at the end," Daniels said last week.

"It's my responsibility, point blank," coach Dan Quinn said.

"It falls on me," offensive coordinator David Blough said.

Whoever takes the largest slice of the blame pie remains open for debate as Washington heads into its MNF kickoff with the 49ers. What's not up for discussion: Just as the Commanders proved they're not ready for a nation's eyes to be on them, they enter a stretch in which four of their next five games stand alone in primetime. Anyone who wants to be watching football will be watching the Commanders, whether they are deserving of that distinction or not.

This is a franchise that has a decidedly tumultuous relationship with primetime football, and one that will spend the next month-and-a-half either proving it is worthy of the country's attention or fading into oblivion once again. Nothing short of the professional futures of the people who run this team hang in the balance, and football fans who care deeply about or are indifferent to the Commanders will get to examine it all in real time.

In the 10 seasons between 2015 and Daniels's rookie year of 2024, only nine teams played fewer regular-season primetime games than Washington.
